response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT circuitId, COUNT(*) AS race_count FROM races GROUP BY circuitId), s AS (SELECT circuitId, race_count, race_count * 1.0 / SUM(race_count) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT circuitId, race_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s), f AS (SELECT circuitId, race_count, share, share - avg_share AS excess_over_avg FROM a WHERE share > avg_share), r AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY excess_over_avg DESC) AS rk FROM f) SELECT circuitId, race_count, share, excess_over_avg FROM r WHERE rk <= 10 ORDER BY excess_over_avg DESC

assumptions.assumption: The average share is taken over all circuits that have at least one race, so it equals 1 divided by the number of such circuits. It is computed before the filter on share.
Top 10 by excess with ties uses RANK(), so every circuit tied with the 10th place is included.
